Description: Identified a pattern that may indicate AWS credentials, risking unauthorized cloud resource access and data breaches on AWS platforms.
Author: bkim4472
Message:
feat(NZAAA-93): Slack nudge worker — C1/C2 queue depth + 1-DM/hr rate-limit (#148)

* feat(NZAAA-93): Slack Bolt nudge worker — C1/C2 queue depth + 1-DM/hr rate-limit

Implements Task 10.4 (GRILL R2-Q9). n8n workflow (every 15 min) reads
awaiting_c1 and awaiting_c2 queue depth via Supabase REST Content-Range,
compares against configurable thresholds (default 5 each, pending Allan SLA
target), and DMs Allan (ALLAN_SLACK_ID) via Slack chat.postMessage when
threshold exceeded. In-memory rate-limit (max 1 DM/queue_type/hr) persisted in
$getWorkflowStaticData so state survives cron restarts. C1 and C2 rate-limits
are fully independent. Fail-safe: Supabase errors suppress DMs rather than
firing spuriously.

Files:
- n8n/workflows/slack-nudge.json — workflow (Cron → fetch×2 → merge → Code → Slack DM → log)
- n8n/workflows/__tests__/slack-nudge.test.ts — 35 unit tests covering all ACs
- n8n/workflows/README.md — env-var contract + design notes for slack-nudge
- apps/n8n/docker-compose.yml — adds C1/C2_QUEUE_DEPTH_THRESHOLD defaults

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-93): sort slack-nudge nodes, publish queue-depth metrics to CloudWatch, correct rate-limit boundary test name

- Sort slack-nudge.json nodes array by id (case-insensitive) so it passes
  scripts/validate-n8n-workflows.ts
- Add Build CloudWatch PutMetricData + PutMetricData to CloudWatch nodes that
  publish C1QueueDepth/C2QueueDepth (namespace NZS/Pipeline, no dimensions)
  unconditionally every tick, matching the alarms in infra/modules/alarms/main.tf
- SigV4-sign in-node via crypto global (no credentials in committed JSON);
  creds from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY env, region AWS_REGION
- Rename the exactly-1-hour rate-limit test to reflect it stays suppressed
  (window is strictly > 1 hour), not 'fires'
- Document new CloudWatch nodes + AWS env vars in README

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-93): address 5 Copilot findings on slack-nudge worker

1. CloudWatch publisher no longer emits a misleading 0 on a Supabase
   read failure — it now publishes only known metrics and skips a
   failed-read metric entirely (returns [] when both reads failed), so
   the queue-depth alarms see genuine missing data rather than a 0 that
   masks a broken system as an empty queue.
2. Credentials now resolve from the EC2 instance profile via IMDSv2
   (the actual infra — no static IAM keys are provisioned for n8n) with
   static env keys as a local/staging override; README corrected to
   describe the instance-profile path instead of required static keys.
3. Added unit tests for the CloudWatch publisher node: skip-on-fetch-
   failure, SigV4 canonical request with session token, IMDS instance-
   profile signing, and the no-credential skip path.
4. Corrected the rate-limit comment that wrongly claimed staticData
   mirrors engagement-event-reader.json (which does not use staticData).
5. The rate-limit timestamp is now stamped by Log DM result only after a
   2xx/ok Slack response, not before the Slack request fires — a failed
   send no longer consumes the 1-hour window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-93): append-mode merge + IMDS hop-limit 2 for container IMDSv2

- Both queues Merge node was in passThrough/single mode, forwarding only one
  branch so the downstream $input.all() saw a single item and the C2 count
  was missing — switch to append mode (mode: append, numberInputs: 2) so both
  Supabase responses pass through as separate items [c1Item, c2Item].
- EC2 metadata_options.http_put_response_hop_limit was 1, but n8n runs in a
  Docker bridge network; the IMDS response TTL hits 0 at the extra container
  hop and is dropped, so the slack-nudge CloudWatch publisher's instance-
  profile credential fetch always returned [] and queue-depth metrics never
  reached the alarms. Raise hop limit to 2 (AWS's documented setting for
  bridge-networked containers; IMDSv2 token still required). Document the
  requirement in the workflows README credential note.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-93): sign CloudWatch SigV4 with Web Crypto, not Node crypto

n8n Code nodes expose the Web Crypto API as the `crypto` global, not Node's
built-in 'crypto' module (and require('crypto') is blocked unless
NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN lists it, which the n8n host does not set). The
CloudWatch PutMetricData node used crypto.createHash / crypto.createHmac, which
are undefined at runtime, so SigV4 signing would have thrown on every tick.

Rewrite the SHA-256 + HMAC-SHA256 signing to crypto.subtle (digest / importKey
+ sign), making the signing path async (the node already awaits IMDS). Update
the test harness to inject the real Web Crypto global instead of Node's crypto
module, so the suite reflects the actual n8n runtime; all 49 slack-nudge tests
still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-93): correct README credential order and Supabase count-query body description

Copilot review findings on PR #148:
- Credential resolution order: the Code node checks static
  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY env keys FIRST and falls back
  to the EC2 instance profile (IMDSv2). The README listed the instance
  profile as #1/default while also saying static keys take precedence —
  internally inconsistent. Reordered so static keys are #1 (checked
  first) and the instance profile is #2 (fallback / production path),
  matching the code.
- Supabase count query: Range: 0-0 asks PostgREST for the first matching
  row, so the body carries a single id row when the queue is non-empty
  (empty array when empty) — not 'no body rows'. The node ignores the
  body and reads the count from Content-Range. Corrected both the
  SUPABASE_URL env-var note and the count_via_content_range design note.

Doc-only change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-93): align queue-depth alarm period with 15-min publish cadence

The slack-nudge worker publishes C1QueueDepth/C2QueueDepth every 15 minutes
(cron */15), but the CloudWatch alarms used period=300 (5 min) with
treat_missing_data=notBreaching. That left two empty 5-minute buckets between
each publish, letting the queue-depth alarms clear or fail to stay in ALARM
between datapoints. Set both alarm periods to 900s so each cron publish lands
in exactly one bucket. Updated the workflow comment to match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-93): make Slack nudge rate-limit adviser-scoped not per-queue

GRILL R2-Q9 specifies max 1 DM per adviser per hour. The rate-limit was
keyed per queue type (c1/c2), so when both awaiting_c1 and awaiting_c2
breached in the same 15-minute tick it sent two separate DMs to Allan —
violating the one-DM-per-hour cap. Allan is the sole adviser (R1-Q15).

The threshold node now takes the most-recent lastDmSentAt across ALL
queues for its suppression decision (adviserRateLimited), and emits at
most one DM per tick (c1 wins when both breach). The downstream Log DM
result node still stamps per-queue timestamps independently. Updated
slack-nudge tests to pin the corrected global behaviour, including a
test that both-breach + c1 DM sent 30 min ago suppresses the c2 DM too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-93): honour threshold 0 and align docs/comments with adviser-scoped rate-limit

- slack-nudge.json: parse C1/C2_QUEUE_DEPTH_THRESHOLD with parseInt+isNaN and accept >= 0 so a configured 0 (DM on any non-empty queue) is honoured instead of silently falling back to 5
- slack-nudge.json: update Log DM result comment to describe the adviser-scoped gate instead of independent windows
- README.md: rewrite the Module 10 summary, the c1_c2_independence design note (now adviser_scoped_rate_limit), and the stamping note to match the adviser-scoped rate-limit (most recent DM across C1/C2 suppresses both for the 1-hour window)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-78): fetch PDF signed URL from ts-service; add s3-signer build step to CI

The ea-app C2 per-run server component called getSignedPdfUrl() from
@nzs/s3-signer directly. That signer needs S3_BUCKET_NAME,
S3_SIGNER_SECRET_ARN and secretsmanager:GetSecretValue — all scoped to the
ts-service ECS task role, not ea-app's. Calling it in ea-app would 500 in ECS.

- Add GET /internal/pdf/signed-url?key=<s3_key> to ts-service (wraps
  getSignedPdfUrl, X-Internal-Secret auth, key constrained to generated/<id>/*.pdf).
- ea-app C2 page now fetches that endpoint via TS_SERVICE_URL +
  TS_SERVICE_INTERNAL_SECRET; null result falls through to PdfNotAvailable.
- Drop @nzs/s3-signer from ea-app deps; add it to ts-service deps.
- Add @nzs/s3-signer to the CI "Build workspace packages" pre-build steps so
  ts-service can resolve it on a clean checkout (no committed dist/).
- Add .env.example entries + ts-service route unit tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-78): wire TS_SERVICE env into ea-app infra; force-dynamic on C2 routes; regen lockfile

- secrets: provision nzs/ts-service/internal-poll-secret (consumers ts_service + ea_app) as the single source of truth for the server-to-server X-Internal-Secret.
- compute/ea_app.tf: inject TS_SERVICE_URL (https://<domain>) + TS_SERVICE_INTERNAL_SECRET; extend the shared execution-role GetSecretValue grant to the new secret ARN.
- compute/ts_service.tf: inject INTERNAL_POLL_SECRET from the same secret so both sides resolve the identical value (previously only consumed in code, never provisioned).
- load_balancer/ts_service.tf: add priority-16 ALB rule forwarding only /internal/pdf/signed-url to ts-service (rest of /internal/* stays off the public ALB) so ea-app can reach the signer endpoint across the ALB.
- ea-app C2 queue + per-run pages: export const dynamic = force-dynamic so the live Supabase query / Date.now() / signed-URL mint run per request.
- pnpm-lock.yaml: restore dropped libc selectors (glibc/musl) on 27 native packages (@next/swc, @rollup, @unrs/resolver) from authoritative registry full-metadata; verified pnpm accepts the lockfile without rewrite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(NZAAA-79): remove c2_processing status update; add cohort_a_no_cv to PipelineStatus

approveC2 previously flipped pipeline_status awaiting_c2 -> c2_processing in
its audit UPDATE. n8n's Phase 4 c2-approve path fans out in parallel (Respond
200 alongside a GET filtered by pipeline_status=eq.awaiting_c2), so that
post-200 UPDATE raced n8n's GET. If the c2_processing write won the race, n8n
found a non-awaiting_c2 row and halted, so the EA email was never sent --
breaking the normal single-adviser happy path, not just the duplicate case.

The action now writes only the c2 audit columns (c2_cleared_at, c2_adviser,
c2_zoom_override, c2_outcome) and never touches pipeline_status; n8n owns the
transition to succeeded. The c2_processing migration is kept (reserved status)
but its comment, the rollback comment, and the actions.ts comments are
rewritten to honestly describe that the C2 double-approval race cannot be fully
prevented client-side; the real protection is n8n's own awaiting_c2 GET guard.

Also add the missing 'cohort_a_no_cv' member to the PipelineStatus union in
pipeline-data.ts (already present in the DB CHECK constraint). Update the test
that asserted pipeline_status: 'c2_processing' to assert the UPDATE no longer
writes pipeline_status while remaining scoped by awaiting_c2.
